policies.title: No new taxes
policies.summary: Commit not to introduce any new taxes in the next term.

policies.title: Compulsory KiwiSaver for workers
policies.summary: Make KiwiSaver or an equivalent scheme compulsory for all workers from 1 July 2028, with combined default contributions rising to 12% by 2032.

policies.title: $1,500 KiwiSaver Baby Boost
policies.summary: Automatically enrol children in KiwiSaver at birth and provide a $1,500 government payment from 1 July 2027.

policies.title: KiwiSaver contribution during paid parental leave
policies.summary: Provide a government KiwiSaver contribution on paid parental leave from 1 July 2027 even when the parent is not contributing.

policies.title: Employer KiwiSaver contributions after 65
policies.summary: Require employers to contribute for participating workers aged over 65 from 1 July 2027.

policies.title: Wider access to 5% first-home deposits
policies.summary: Raise the First Home Loan income cap to $300,000 for all applicants so more buyers can use a 5% deposit.

policies.title: Extend paid parental leave to 30 weeks
policies.summary: Increase paid parental leave from 26 to 30 weeks in stages over the next term.

policies.title: Shared and overlapping parental leave
policies.summary: Allow parents to take paid parental leave together or in overlapping instalments.

policies.title: Full holiday pay after parental leave
policies.summary: Protect annual leave accrual during parental leave and full-rate holiday pay after returning to work.

policies.title: Lower domestic student-loan repayment rate
policies.summary: Reduce the compulsory repayment rate for New Zealand-based borrowers from 12% to 10% from 1 April 2027.

policies.title: Tougher overseas student-loan recovery
policies.summary: Increase penalties and enforcement for serious student-loan default by borrowers living overseas.

policies.title: Budget Responsibility Rules
policies.summary: Target surplus in 2028/29, keep debt moving toward and below 40% of GDP, and reduce core Crown spending toward 30% of GDP.

policies.title: Home Energy Fund
policies.summary: Offer ten-year, low-interest, property-secured loans repaid through rates to ratepayers with at least 20% equity, for solar, batteries, insulation, heat pumps and other home electrification.

policies.title: National rules for small renewables
policies.summary: Make small-scale solar, micro-hydro and battery storage largely permitted as of right through national planning rules.

policies.title: Rooftop solar without consent
policies.summary: Allow rooftop solar without resource consent even where height limits or landscape overlays would otherwise apply.

policies.title: Permitted small-scale on-farm solar
policies.summary: Make small on-farm ground-mounted solar a permitted activity subject to standard environmental safeguards.

policies.title: $100m annual conservation funding from visitor levy
policies.summary: Direct $100 million a year from the International Visitor Levy to the Department of Conservation.

policies.title: $50m Tourism Priorities Fund
policies.summary: Ring-fence $50 million a year for tourism growth, resilience, marketing, events, infrastructure, data and workforce needs.

policies.title: Share visitor-levy revenue with councils
policies.summary: Distribute remaining International Visitor Levy revenue to councils according to international guest nights.

policies.title: Hold visitor levy for three years
policies.summary: Commit not to increase the International Visitor Levy for at least three years.

policies.title: Engineer sign-off for commercial work
policies.summary: Let qualified engineers sign off specified commercial building work without a duplicate council inspection.

policies.title: Specialist national building consent authority
policies.summary: Create a dedicated pathway for large commercial building consents with specialist expertise and nationally consistent decisions.

policies.title: Trade negotiations with seven economies
policies.summary: Begin trade negotiations with seven new economies across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia within five years.

policies.title: Essential-supplies agreements
policies.summary: Negotiate supply-security agreements with like-minded partners using the New Zealand–Singapore agreement as a model.

policies.title: Paperless trade and digital customs
policies.summary: Expand paperless trade and digital customs and target $1 billion of non-tariff barriers.

policies.title: Export growth and trade missions
policies.summary: Run at least 23 commercially focused trade missions next term and retain the target of doubling export value by 2034.

policies.title: Rolleston freight-hub connections
policies.summary: Invest $50 million in shared road and rail connections for the Rolleston intermodal freight hub.

policies.title: Queenstown transport upgrades
policies.summary: Make gondola proposals eligible for public transport funding and commit $25 million to four-lane the remaining route to Five Mile roundabout.

policies.title: Replace the RMA and change pastoral-land settings
policies.summary: Complete the RMA replacement and enable high-country farmers to invest and diversify under new Crown pastoral-land settings.

policies.title: Visitor access charges at Aoraki and Milford Sound
policies.summary: Introduce international-visitor access charges at Aoraki / Mt Cook and Milford Sound for local conservation and tourism infrastructure.

policies.title: National mining and quarry standards
policies.summary: Issue a mining policy statement and national standards for river gravel extraction and on-farm quarries.

policies.title: New data centres to bring firm generation
policies.summary: Require new data-centre projects to be accompanied by new firmed electricity generation.

policies.title: Complete Christchurch Hospital Tower Three
policies.summary: Finish the fit-out of Tower Three at Christchurch Hospital, adding 96 beds.

policies.title: Complete funded South Island classrooms
policies.summary: Deliver nearly 100 funded teaching spaces and complete redevelopment work across 14 South Island schools.

policies.title: Recognise valued introduced species
policies.summary: Create a coordinated wild-animal management framework and legally recognise introduced species with recreational, economic, environmental or cultural value.

policies.title: Strengthen Game Animal Council and modernise Fish & Game
policies.summary: Give the Game Animal Council a clearer management role and simplify Fish & Game administration and accountability.

policies.title: Expand hunter-led conservation
policies.summary: Invite proposals for more herds of special interest and replace the 1993 Tahr Control Plan with a modern plan developed with hunters.

policies.title: Protect hunting and fishing access
policies.summary: Open suitable Crown land to hunting and fishing and protect practical recreational access when sensitive land is sold overseas.

policies.title: Grow hunting-related jobs and exports
policies.summary: Promote guided hunting overseas and simplify trophy export, veterinary, taxidermy and customs processes.

policies.title: Modernise sexual consent laws
policies.summary: Define consent as actively communicated by words or actions, while retaining the prosecution's obligation to prove beyond reasonable doubt that consent was not given and the defendant lacked reasonable grounds to believe it was.

policies.title: Pursue separation of Foodstuffs
policies.summary: Ask the Commerce Commission to assess whether Foodstuffs should be separated into competing New World/Four Square and Pak'nSave chains, and legislate if the Commission recommends separation as beneficial to shoppers.

policies.title: Auckland Transport Police Team
policies.summary: Fund 50 additional sworn officers at $7 million a year from Budget 2027 for a dedicated police presence across Auckland trains, buses, ferries and major transport hubs.

policies.title: Under-16 social-media and online-safety rules
policies.summary: Ban under-16s from high-risk social-media platforms, require age checks and child-safety risk assessments, regulate AI companion platforms, and create an independent online-safety regulator.

policies.title: $20 city and $10 regional weekly fare caps
policies.summary: From 1 July 2027, cap weekly public-transport fares at $20 in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and $10 elsewhere. Include buses, trains and some ferries, excluding interregional and scenic services.

policies.title: Three free GP visits each year
policies.summary: Provide every eligible New Zealander with three free doctor's visits a year through a Medicard.

policies.title: Free prescriptions
policies.summary: Remove the $5 prescription charge for everyone from 1 July 2027.

policies.title: Free maternity scans
policies.summary: Make maternity scans free nationwide through the Medicard from July 2028.

policies.title: New Zealand Future Fund
policies.summary: Create a public investment fund to back New Zealand businesses and productive domestic investment.

policies.title: Free cervical screening
policies.summary: Provide free cervical screening for people aged 25–69 from 1 October 2027.

policies.title: Family Doctor Loan Scheme
policies.summary: Support local GPs to buy into practices and remain in their communities, starting 1 July 2027.

policies.title: 28% capital gains tax on investment property
policies.summary: Tax profits earned after 1 July 2027 when commercial or residential investment property is sold, while excluding the family home and specified other assets.

policies.title: Expanded Apprenticeship Boost
policies.summary: Extend employer payments, add a $1,000 toolbox grant and cover five additional trades.

policies.title: SolarSaver
policies.summary: Help homeowners, renters and communities install solar through subsidies, low-cost finance and community batteries without upfront cost.

policies.title: Paid-on-time rules
policies.summary: Require large businesses to pay small suppliers within 15 days for invoices of $25,000 or less and publish payment times, with reporting and proportionate penalties for late payment.

policies.title: Higher instant asset write-off
policies.summary: Make it easier for small firms to deduct qualifying investment costs immediately.

policies.title: Higher GST registration threshold
policies.summary: Raise the GST threshold to reduce compliance for the smallest businesses.

policies.title: Small Business First procurement
policies.summary: Set a target for 15% of government contracts to go to New Zealand small businesses and start-ups, break suitable large contracts into smaller jobs, and reduce repeated government paperwork.

policies.title: Return to surplus and reduce net debt
policies.summary: Return to OBEGAL surplus in 2028/29 and bring net debt below 20% of GDP over time while holding the operating allowance at $2.4 billion per Budget.

policies.title: Parliamentary Budget Office
policies.summary: Establish an independent Parliamentary Budget Office for fiscal transparency.

policies.title: Restore Reserve Bank dual mandate
policies.summary: Restore maximum sustainable employment alongside price stability as a Reserve Bank mandate.

policies.title: Restore wellbeing reporting
policies.summary: Restore wellbeing reporting requirements to the Public Finance Act.

policies.title: Office of AI
policies.summary: Create a government Office of AI to coordinate policy and national capability.

policies.title: Online safety regulator
policies.summary: Establish an independent digital regulator with powers to enforce safety standards, investigate harmful practices and act against online platforms that break the rules.

policies.title: AI copyright and creator payments
policies.summary: Develop a framework to recognise and pay creators when AI systems use their work.

policies.title: Data centres pay their own infrastructure costs
policies.summary: Require data centres to meet their own energy and water infrastructure costs.

policies.title: Māori-led skilled-work training
policies.summary: Invest $21 million a year in Māori-led practical training, mentoring and employer connections.

policies.title: Graduate nurse job guarantee
policies.summary: Offer every eligible New Zealand-trained graduate registered or enrolled nurse a health-system job from 2027.

policies.title: Compulsory employer KiwiSaver contributions to 6%
policies.summary: Make employer contributions compulsory from 1 July 2028 and raise them to 6% by 2032.

policies.title: KiwiSaver support during parental leave
policies.summary: Provide a new KiwiSaver contribution for parents receiving paid parental leave.

policies.title: Employer KiwiSaver contributions after 65
policies.summary: Extend compulsory employer contributions to employees working past age 65 from 1 July 2028.

policies.title: Ban new total-remuneration KiwiSaver contracts
policies.summary: Prevent new employment contracts from absorbing compulsory employer KiwiSaver contributions into total remuneration.

policies.title: Ban price gouging for essential goods and services
policies.summary: Make it illegal for large companies with substantial market power to charge excessive prices for essentials or pay suppliers unfairly low prices, with Commerce Commission investigations, penalties and customer repayments.

policies.title: Children and whānau
policies.summary: Put tamariki, rangatahi and whānau first, with support aimed at safety, connection and freedom from poverty.

policies.title: Emissions reduction
policies.summary: Cut climate pollution, make large polluters pay and rapidly phase out fossil fuels while electrifying the economy.

policies.title: Climate resilience and adaptation
policies.summary: Prepare communities for severe weather and support people through adaptation and the zero-emissions transition.

policies.title: Conservation and biodiversity
policies.summary: Protect and restore indigenous species, forests, waterways and ecosystems from exploitation.

policies.title: Culture and creativity
policies.summary: Increase support for artists, creative work, cultural organisations, training and access.

policies.title: Democracy reform
policies.summary: Reduce the influence of wealthy and corporate interests and strengthen representative democratic rules.

policies.title: Digital technology
policies.summary: Regulate digital platforms to protect wellbeing, privacy, information and democratic control.

policies.title: Disability rights and services
policies.summary: Improve accessible housing, transport and services and support disabled people and whānau to live with autonomy.

policies.title: Health-based drug law reform
policies.summary: Shift alcohol and other drug policy from punishment toward evidence-based health and harm reduction.

policies.title: Inclusive public education
policies.summary: Support an inclusive, well-resourced public education system that promotes lifelong learning.

policies.title: Affordable renewable energy
policies.summary: Restructure the power system around public benefit, renewable supply and lower household costs.

policies.title: Environmental protection
policies.summary: Strengthen protections for clean water, forests, wetlands, soil and air.

policies.title: Food, fibre and forestry
policies.summary: Support regenerative farming and forestry, food security, mātauranga Māori and healthy rural communities.

policies.title: Healthy freshwater
policies.summary: Restore rivers and lakes for drinking, swimming and gathering kai, placing ecological and community health first.

policies.title: Gender equity
policies.summary: Advance equality, safety and economic security for women and gender minorities.

policies.title: Global affairs and trade
policies.summary: Pursue an independent foreign policy focused on peace, human rights, climate action and fair trade.

policies.title: Accessible public healthcare
policies.summary: Increase equitable access to timely care and support the health workforce and public system.

policies.title: Safe and affordable homes
policies.summary: Increase secure, warm and affordable housing and treat housing as a basic right rather than a speculative asset.

policies.title: Immigration and refugees
policies.summary: Provide fair, safe pathways for migrants and refugees and protect migrant workers from exploitation.

policies.title: Liveable incomes and fair tax
policies.summary: Guarantee adequate incomes and fund services through higher taxes on extreme wealth and large corporations, alongside income-tax cuts for most people.

policies.title: Justice and community safety
policies.summary: Prioritise prevention, rehabilitation and action on the causes of crime while reforming inequitable justice settings.

policies.title: Empowered local government
policies.summary: Improve council funding and democratic participation so local government can deliver housing, resilience and community wellbeing.

policies.title: Māori-centred services and authority
policies.summary: Support Māori decision-making and kaupapa Māori approaches for whānau, hapū and iwi.

policies.title: Accessible mental-health care
policies.summary: Address drivers of distress and provide timely, culturally relevant community and clinical support.

policies.title: Oceans and fisheries
policies.summary: Expand marine protection, restore fisheries and restrict destructive practices such as bottom trawling.

policies.title: Support overseas New Zealanders
policies.summary: Keep expatriate New Zealanders connected and treat their student loans and civic participation fairly.

policies.title: Pacific partnership
policies.summary: Strengthen Pacific relationships and reduce systemic barriers facing Pacific communities in New Zealand.

policies.title: Reverse National's public-service cuts
policies.summary: Cancel National's proposed $2.4 billion in public-service cuts and invest in a strong, well-resourced public sector.

policies.title: Rainbow communities
policies.summary: Protect the safety, healthcare, rights and full participation of rainbow communities.

policies.title: Support for seniors
policies.summary: Improve access to care, connection, housing and income support so older people can live with dignity.

policies.title: Support local enterprise
policies.summary: Back small local businesses, sustainable industries and fair access to markets and procurement.

policies.title: Te Tiriti o Waitangi
policies.summary: Put Te Tiriti partnership and rangatiratanga at the centre of governance and public decision-making.

policies.title: Tertiary education overhaul
policies.summary: Improve funding, student support and access across universities, polytechnics and other tertiary pathways.

policies.title: Affordable sustainable transport
policies.summary: Invest in frequent public transport, passenger rail, walking and cycling and reduce transport costs and emissions.

policies.title: Violence prevention
policies.summary: Strengthen prevention, survivor support and trauma recovery for family, sexual and community violence.

policies.title: Welfare of animals
policies.summary: Tighten animal welfare standards and enforcement to reduce cruelty and suffering.

policies.title: Workforce rights
policies.summary: Strengthen employment protections, collective voice, pay and working conditions.

policies.title: Zero waste and circular economy
policies.summary: Reduce waste and plastic pollution and require producers to take responsibility for products and packaging.

policies.title: $50 million a year for te reo Māori
policies.summary: Provide $30 million a year for teacher education and professional development in te reo Māori and $20 million a year for Te Taura Whiri and Te Mātāwai.

policies.title: KiwiMart and affordable-food package
policies.summary: Create a publicly owned supermarket chain by acquiring at least 120 stores and distribution capacity, prohibit excessive grocery pricing, strengthen the Commerce Commission, fund community food security and expand school lunches.

policies.title: An easier end to employment
policies.summary: Simplify employment termination rules and reduce procedural risk for employers.

policies.title: Voluntary university student-services fees
policies.summary: Make university student-services fees voluntary, allowing students to choose which services they pay for.

policies.title: Affordable school uniforms
policies.summary: Limit compulsory branded school-uniform items and allow families to buy generic basics from ordinary retailers.

policies.title: Local Tourism Dividend
policies.summary: Pay councils $1 per commercial guest night from existing revenue, without a new bed tax, to help fund visitor-related infrastructure.

policies.title: Scrap net zero and cut the carbon tax
policies.summary: Repeal the Zero Carbon Act, remove the domestic net-zero target and reduce costs imposed through the Emissions Trading Scheme.

policies.title: Unlock the digital economy
policies.summary: Coordinate ministerial responsibility across digital-economy work programmes and remove regulatory barriers to digital business, innovation and investment.

policies.title: Disestablish the Climate Change Commission
policies.summary: Abolish the Climate Change Commission and move climate decisions back to elected government.

policies.title: Smaller and more affordable government
policies.summary: Consolidate ministries, reduce ministerial portfolios and public-service administration, and strengthen ministerial accountability.

policies.title: Independent certification for health-related benefits
policies.summary: Require health and disability benefit certification through an MSD-approved pool using objective criteria and phased reassessment.

policies.title: Managed payments after four months on Jobseeker
policies.summary: Use an electronic card for long-term work-ready Jobseeker recipients, directing payments to essentials and blocking specified purchases.

policies.title: Innovation trials
policies.summary: Create a pathway for innovators to test products and services under time-limited regulatory exemptions and safeguards.

policies.title: Put 'reside' back in resident
policies.summary: Replace indefinite resident travel rights with a five-year travel facility requiring 730 days in New Zealand within a rolling five-year period, with specified exemptions. Existing permanent residents would not be affected.

policies.title: Keeping children safe
policies.summary: Introduce a national safety card for people working or volunteering with children, with ongoing police checks, training and safeguards including suspension following serious charges.

policies.title: Deport serious offenders
policies.summary: Broaden deportation consequences for non-citizens convicted of serious offending.

policies.title: Three Strikes for burglary
policies.summary: Require at least three years’ imprisonment without parole for a third burglary conviction.

policies.title: Stop coercion through animal abuse
policies.summary: Recognise and address threats or harm to animals used to control victims of family violence.

policies.title: Keep public spaces safe
policies.summary: Give authorities additional tools to address persistent intimidation, disorder and unsafe behaviour in public places.

policies.title: Rural crime crackdown
policies.summary: Fund 100,000 additional rural Police patrol hours each year, establish a dedicated rural crime unit, expand rural Text 111 access, strengthen inter-agency coordination, and increase penalties for livestock theft and poaching.

policies.title: A Starship for cancer
policies.summary: Establish National Cancer Centre campuses in Auckland and Christchurch, subject to a business case, backed by an approximately $2 billion fiscal contingency and an independent philanthropic foundation.

policies.title: Let pharmacies do more
policies.summary: Fund pharmacists to provide medication reviews, appropriate blood tests and routine monitoring, with information shared with GPs, alongside more routine medicines and minor-ailment care.

policies.title: Strengthen End of Life Choice
policies.summary: Expand or simplify access to assisted dying under the End of Life Choice framework.

policies.title: Close the medicines gap
policies.summary: Increase medicines’ share of the health budget by one percentage point each year until it reaches Australia’s level in 2033.

policies.title: Wind up the Waitangi Tribunal
policies.summary: End the Waitangi Tribunal after historical claims are completed and move remaining issues to ordinary institutions.

policies.title: One public service for all
policies.summary: Require public services and employment decisions to be based on individual need and merit rather than ancestry.

policies.title: One law for all
policies.summary: Add parliamentary sovereignty, the rule of law and equality before the law to the Constitution Act, and add property rights to the New Zealand Bill of Rights Act.

policies.title: Free speech for regulated professionals
policies.summary: Stop professional regulators disciplining lawful private expression and require political neutrality in regulation and training.

policies.title: No votes for unelected representatives
policies.summary: Reserve voting rights on council committees for elected members while allowing consultation and advice from others.

policies.title: Keep New Zealand moving
policies.summary: Prioritise practical road and transport investment and reduce delays to network delivery.

policies.title: A fair contribution for infrastructure
policies.summary: Introduce a $6-per-day infrastructure surcharge for people on temporary work visas.

policies.title: Grazing to cut pests and fire risk
policies.summary: Allow controlled grazing on suitable public land to reduce weeds, pests and wildfire fuel.

policies.title: Change the Paris framework
policies.summary: Seek fairer international climate commitments and reconsider New Zealand's participation in the Paris Agreement if overseas competitors avoid costs imposed on New Zealand farmers.

policies.title: Rural workforce visa
policies.summary: Create a visa pathway tailored to persistent workforce shortages in farming and rural industries.

policies.title: Disrupt the class, leave the class
policies.summary: Make it easier to remove persistently disruptive students from a classroom while arranging appropriate alternatives.

policies.title: Let the kid on the bus
policies.summary: Allow rural students to use school-bus services that pass their homes with spare seats.

policies.title: Equal treatment at universities
policies.summary: Require publicly funded university support to be based on merit or need rather than race, while allowing privately funded targeted scholarships.

policies.title: Fisheries management and abundance
policies.summary: Reform fisheries management, including Hauraki Gulf management, shellfish catch limits, scallop dredging and fisheries levies.

policies.title: Protect lawful hunting
policies.summary: Create stronger legal protections against dangerous interference with lawful hunting.

policies.title: Open the backcountry
policies.summary: Improve hunting access through clearer helicopter landing rules, a stronger Game Animal Council role and changes to commercial venison recovery regulation.

policies.title: Back conservation volunteers
policies.summary: Direct more support and authority to volunteer hunting and conservation groups.

policies.title: Hunter-led game management
policies.summary: Put hunters in charge of game-animal management within defined conservation limits while retaining DOC's wider role.

policies.title: Freeze the adult minimum wage for three years
policies.summary: Hold the adult minimum wage at its current rate for three years.

policies.title: Under-20 training wage at 60%
policies.summary: Set a training wage at 60% of the adult minimum wage for workers under 20 during their first 12 months with an employer.

policies.title: Protected employment-exit discussions
policies.summary: Allow employers and employees to begin protected exit negotiations without the conversation itself triggering a personal grievance.

policies.title: Shorter personal-grievance filing period
policies.summary: Shorten the time allowed to lodge a personal grievance with the Employment Relations Authority.

policies.title: Voluntary union-fee payroll deductions
policies.summary: End compulsory employer collection of union membership fees and make payroll deductions voluntary.

policies.title: Restrict birthright citizenship
policies.summary: Automatically grant citizenship at birth only to children of New Zealand citizens.

policies.title: Temporary protected-person status
policies.summary: Make asylum protection temporary and subject to ongoing review, with tighter rules for claimants on work visas.

policies.title: Longer residence and citizenship qualifying periods
policies.summary: Increase the permanent-residence qualifying period from two to five years and citizenship from five to ten years.

policies.title: Higher residence and citizenship application fees
policies.summary: Increase application charges to fund the immigration system and reflect the value placed on status.

policies.title: Ten-year benefit stand-down for visa holders
policies.summary: Make non-citizens ineligible for Jobseeker, Accommodation Supplement and other benefits during their first ten years in New Zealand.

policies.title: Broader deportation rules
policies.summary: Allow deportation for any imprisonable offence and automatic deportation for specified violent, sexual, fraud and organised-crime offences.

policies.title: Referendum on a 20,000 resident-visa cap
policies.summary: Hold a referendum on an annual resident-visa cap of 20,000 linked to infrastructure capacity and a 30-year population plan.

policies.title: Social housing for citizens first
policies.summary: Prioritise New Zealand citizens for social housing.

policies.title: Overstayer self-deportation and Pacific clemency
policies.summary: Offer a 24-month self-deportation period, a pathway for Pacific overstayers to regularise status, and permanent exclusion after the deadline for others found unlawfully present.

policies.title: Student visa holders reapply offshore
policies.summary: Require international students seeking another visa to leave New Zealand and apply from abroad.

policies.title: End automatic work rights for international students
policies.summary: Require international students to apply separately and meet strict conditions before working.

policies.title: NZ Super for citizens only
policies.summary: From 2029, restrict New Zealand Superannuation eligibility to New Zealand citizens.

policies.title: Oppose an under-16 social-media ban
policies.summary: Do not support legislation banning social media for under-16s because of privacy, enforcement and parental-rights concerns.

policies.title: Use It or Lose It dairy policy
policies.summary: Give qualifying new value-added dairy manufacturers access to up to 500 million litres of Fonterra milk a year on a tapering ten-year basis.

policies.title: Kiwi Kids Grant
policies.summary: Pay a tax-free $5,000 a year for each of the first three children during their first three years, where at least one parent is a citizen.

policies.title: Accessibility Standards Bill
policies.summary: Create practical national standards to identify, prevent and remove avoidable accessibility barriers.

policies.title: Citizens-only voting
policies.summary: Change electoral law so only New Zealand citizens, rather than all permanent residents, may vote.

policies.title: Disestablish Auckland's Independent Māori Statutory Board
policies.summary: Remove Auckland Council's unelected Independent Māori Statutory Board.

policies.title: Marsden Point Special Economic Zone
policies.summary: Create a special economic zone at Marsden Point to support exports, industry and national resilience.

policies.title: Buy back BNZ and combine with Kiwibank
policies.summary: Return the Bank of New Zealand to public ownership and combine it with Kiwibank as a larger New Zealand-owned bank.

policies.title: Nationwide container-return scheme
policies.summary: Introduce deposits and refunds for beverage containers to improve recycling and shift clean-up costs from ratepayers.

policies.title: Break up the supermarket duopoly
policies.summary: Split Foodstuffs into competing New World/Four Square and Pak'nSave businesses, alongside Woolworths, to increase supermarket competition.

policies.title: Define woman and man in legislation
policies.summary: Add sex-based definitions of woman and man to New Zealand legislation.

policies.title: Return 50% of mining royalties to regions
policies.summary: Allocate half of Crown mining royalties to the region where extraction occurs.

policies.title: $15m more for Christ Church Cathedral
policies.summary: Provide an additional $15 million toward the Christ Church Cathedral rebuild.

policies.title: Split major electricity gentailers
policies.summary: Separate generation and retail operations of the four major power companies to increase competition and reduce household power costs.

policies.title: Inquiry into vaccine injuries
policies.summary: Hold a select committee inquiry into injuries alleged to have followed mandated COVID-19 vaccination.

policies.title: Make English an official language
policies.summary: Legislate English as an official language of New Zealand.

policies.title: Bank liability for payment scams
policies.summary: Require banks to do more to prevent payment scams and compensate eligible victims.

policies.title: Binding referendum on Māori electorates
policies.summary: Hold a binding referendum at the 2026 election on whether the Māori electorates should continue.

policies.title: Te Tiriti Entrenchment
policies.summary: Create a Matike Mai Fund, implement UNDRIP, establish an independent Te Tiriti Commission and make Waitangi Tribunal recommendations binding.

policies.title: Fairer tax on wealth
policies.summary: Increase the contribution from the wealthiest and use the revenue for housing, health, education and whānau support.

policies.title: Kai sovereignty
policies.summary: Protect Māori food and seed systems, oppose genetically engineered food, support Māori-owned supermarkets and regenerative agriculture, and improve access to land.

policies.title: Mokopuna Māori
policies.summary: End state practices that separate Māori children from whānau, invest in whānau-led care and strengthen accountability for harmful uplifts and placements.

policies.title: Māori-led disability services
policies.summary: Fund accessible Māori-led disability services and decision-making shaped around whānau realities.

policies.title: Public, affordable and whenua Māori housing
policies.summary: Build more public and affordable homes, make building on ancestral land easier, and act on speculation, vacant homes and land banking.

policies.title: Māori-led education and training
policies.summary: Create Māori-led authority and solutions, embed mātauranga Māori and remove barriers to education and training.

policies.title: Toi Māori
policies.summary: Invest in Māori creative industries, protect cultural expression and support Māori-led arts infrastructure and pathways.

policies.title: Te reo Māori revitalisation
policies.summary: Strengthen te reo Māori learning and community-led revitalisation and make the state accountable for its protection.

policies.title: Māori-led health authority and services
policies.summary: Rebuild Māori-led health authority, shift toward prevention and whānau wellbeing, and make care culturally safe and accountable.

policies.title: Mana motuhake
policies.summary: Advance Te Tiriti-based constitutional change, Māori political authority, land return and rangatiratanga commitments.

policies.title: Community sport pathways
policies.summary: Invest in local clubs, programmes and facilities that build belonging, wellbeing and opportunity for rangatahi.

policies.title: Māori-led justice transformation
policies.summary: Create Māori-led justice authority and community solutions, reform laws that criminalise poverty and move away from mass imprisonment.

policies.title: Māori economic development
policies.summary: Create Māori-led funds and institutions for enterprise, trade, innovation, long-term wealth and data sovereignty.

policies.title: Lift incomes and strengthen welfare
policies.summary: Increase incomes, strengthen welfare and provide practical transport and cost-of-living relief.

policies.title: Military neutrality
policies.summary: Declare military neutrality, review military alignments and refocus defence on protection, disaster response and Pacific support.

policies.title: Māori authority over freshwater
policies.summary: Require Māori consent and authority in freshwater decisions and share benefits while protecting wai.

policies.title: $1 billion Energy Sovereignty Fund
policies.summary: Establish a $1 billion fund to build Māori and community-owned energy assets.

policies.title: Stronger energy-market regulators
policies.summary: Give energy-market regulators stronger powers to act against excessive pricing and profits.

policies.title: Abundant Energy
policies.summary: Add up to 30 GW of renewable generation by 2050, reform electricity regulation and distributors, reinvest government power-company profits, and support household, community and business electrification.

policies.title: Breakthrough Economy
policies.summary: Lift research and development investment, strengthen Commerce Commission powers against uncompetitive markets, and expand practical support for innovators and small businesses.

policies.title: Clean Up Politics
policies.summary: Regulate lobbying, tighten political-donation rules, create an independent anti-corruption body, strengthen transparency laws and prohibit misleading election advertising.

policies.title: Healthy Oceans
policies.summary: Move fisheries toward ecosystem-based management, phase out bottom trawling, oppose seabed mining, expand marine protection and invest in a sustainable blue economy.

policies.title: Tax Reset
policies.summary: Introduce a Citizen's Income, a land value tax and compulsory KiwiSaver 2.0 as a combined package intended to lift incomes, reduce property speculation and strengthen retirement saving.

policies.title: Citizens' Voice
policies.summary: Use representative, paid citizens' assemblies for major long-term issues and establish an independent Parliamentary Commissioner to convene and support them.

policies.title: Future-fit Education
policies.summary: Create a 10-year cross-party education plan led by an independent council, improve teacher support and workforce planning, and modernise learning for future needs.

policies.title: Healthy People
policies.summary: Create a costed 10-year cross-party health plan, advocate lifting health funding to 9% of GDP, expand primary and preventive care, and protect policy from harmful-industry influence.

policies.title: Honouring Te Tiriti
policies.summary: Honour and complete Treaty settlements, restore earlier customary marine-title settings, strengthen Treaty analysis in lawmaking and support Māori-led services and economic development.

policies.title: Smart on Crime
policies.summary: Invest earlier in at-risk young people, expand specialist and restorative-justice programmes, address drivers of offending, improve reintegration and regulate recreational cannabis.

policies.title: Affordable Housing
policies.summary: Use a land value tax to curb land banking and combine it with a large-scale house-building programme aimed at reducing the national housing shortage.

policies.title: Inter-Generational Infrastructure
policies.summary: Put the 30-year National Infrastructure Plan into law, strengthen independent oversight, prioritise maintenance and use funding approaches suited to long-lived assets.

policies.title: Climate Action
policies.summary: Strengthen the Emissions Trading Scheme, include agricultural emissions, exclude new exotic forestry, support adaptation and reward nature-rich carbon storage such as soils and wetlands.

policies.title: Healthy Land
policies.summary: Increase conservation and biosecurity funding, strengthen water-quality oversight, support lower-impact land use and develop nature markets, native forestry and a circular plastics economy.

policies.title: Industry Energy Resilience Fund
policies.summary: Create a ring-fenced fund for industrial electrification, capitalised by a $1 billion green bond backed by future ETS auction revenue, using loans, guarantees and targeted grants.

policies.title: Protect the Climate Change Commission
policies.summary: Oppose abolishing the Climate Change Commission and protect independent climate oversight in any government Opportunity supports.

policies.title: Send the online safety bill to select committee
policies.summary: Support the Online Safety (Minimum Age and Child Safety Risk Assessment) Bill at first reading, while seeking stronger platform duties and reserving a final position until evidence and privacy issues are examined.

policies.title: Reverse the charitable-donation tax-credit cap
policies.summary: Repeal the $100,000 cap on donations eligible for the 33% tax credit and ask the Law Commission to review charitable regulation.

policies.title: Risk-based gene technology framework
policies.summary: Withdraw the current Gene Technology Bill and replace it with case-by-case, risk-based regulation, independent expert assessment, clear liability and a citizens' assembly.

policies.title: Targeted tax incentives for business EVs
policies.summary: Allow full first-year depreciation and a two-year fringe-benefit-tax exemption for qualifying new business EVs, capped by vehicle price and ending in 2030.

policies.title: Permanent free public transport
policies.summary: Introduce permanent, universal fare-free public transport across New Zealand, with an estimated net cost of about $150 million a year after ticketing-system savings.

policies.title: Capacity-based immigration planning
policies.summary: Set immigration goals through a Government Policy Statement reflecting workforce, demographic, housing and infrastructure needs.

policies.title: Four-year path to permanent residence
policies.summary: Extend the residence period before permanent-residence eligibility from two years to four, supported by New Zealand orientation and civic education.

policies.title: Change accredited employers after three months
policies.summary: Allow migrant workers to move between accredited employers after three months, alongside stronger Accredited Employer Work Visa protections and community support.

policies.title: Protect humanitarian deportation appeals
policies.summary: Protect access to humanitarian appeals against deportation.

policies.title: Citizenship pathway for New Zealand-born children
policies.summary: Create a citizenship pathway for children born in New Zealand who do not receive citizenship automatically at birth.

policies.title: Human decisions on welfare payments
policies.summary: Prohibit artificial intelligence and automated systems from cancelling, suspending or reducing welfare payments or imposing benefit sanctions, and retain access to a human decision-maker.

policies.title: Compulsory workforce KiwiSaver
policies.summary: Make KiwiSaver compulsory for the workforce and increase employee and employer contributions to 8% initially and eventually 10%.

policies.title: $1,000 KiwiSaver start at birth
policies.summary: Automatically enrol New Zealand citizen children in KiwiSaver at birth with an immediate $1,000 Crown contribution.

policies.title: Permanently ban seabed mining
policies.summary: Support the proposed Seabed Mining Prohibition Act 2026 to establish a permanent legislative ban on seabed mining in New Zealand waters.

policies.title: Publicly owned Kiwipower
policies.summary: Establish a publicly owned electricity generator to invest in renewable generation, improve energy security and support new independent market participants.

policies.title: Zero-interest clean-energy loans
policies.summary: Offer zero-interest loans for household solar panels and battery storage.

policies.title: Renters' right to solar
policies.summary: Create a renters' right to solar and legalise plug-in solar systems.

policies.title: Expand Warmer Kiwi Homes
policies.summary: Expand Warmer Kiwi Homes to cover more energy-efficiency upgrades, including transitions away from gas, with a focus on low-income households.

policies.title: $200 million for community renewable energy
policies.summary: Invest $200 million in community-owned renewable-energy projects such as solar for schools, marae, papakāinga and libraries.

policies.title: Solar for public and Māori housing
policies.summary: Install solar on more than half of public homes within four years and invest $80 million in renewable energy for Māori housing.

policies.title: Ban good-character sentencing discounts for sexual offending
policies.summary: Prohibit judges from treating an offender's good character or public reputation as a mitigating factor when sentencing sexual offences.

policies.title: Independent curriculum and assessment council
policies.summary: Establish an Independent Council for Curriculum and Assessment in legislation, with an interim expert group appointed within the first three months.

policies.title: One-year pause for unimplemented curriculum changes
policies.summary: Pause curriculum changes that have not yet been implemented for one year while expert advice is obtained, while continuing mathematics and English work already underway.

policies.title: Keep the current NCEA system until 2029
policies.summary: Keep the current NCEA system unchanged until 2029 so expert advice can be considered and any later changes can be planned and phased.

policies.title: End restrictive supermarket contracts
policies.summary: End supermarket contracts that prevent individual stores from lowering prices, changing chains or becoming independent.

policies.title: Ban supermarket supplier junk fees
policies.summary: Ban supermarket fees charged to food producers for services that provide no real value, and simplify rebates and data charges.

policies.title: Guarantee wholesale supply for smaller grocers
policies.summary: Guarantee smaller supermarkets and grocers access to wholesale supply that cannot be withdrawn because they grow or compete more strongly.

policies.title: Create two independent grocery wholesalers
policies.summary: Create independently run Foodstuffs Wholesale and Woolworths Wholesale businesses to supply competing supermarkets and grocers.

policies.title: Stronger electricity competition enforcement
policies.summary: Put electricity-market competition and fair access first and strengthen enforcement when companies misuse market power to block better consumer deals.

policies.title: Choose who buys household-generated power
policies.summary: Allow households generating electricity to sell their surplus to the buyer offering the best deal rather than requiring them to use their retail supplier.

policies.title: Private investment in electricity transmission
policies.summary: Allow private investors to build, own and operate transmission connected to the National Grid when common technical and reliability standards are met.

policies.title: Competitive electricity connection work
policies.summary: Allow qualified providers to compete to deliver customer-funded electricity connection work for homes, developments and businesses.

policies.title: Alternatives must compete with new electricity lines
policies.summary: Require batteries, flexible connections and demand-response options to compete with expensive electricity-network upgrades where they can meet the same need.

policies.title: Property-rights rules for the RMA replacement
policies.summary: Put property rights first in national rules replacing the RMA, using clear measurable standards focused on actual environmental harm and local conditions.

policies.title: Remove Te Mana o te Wai
policies.summary: Remove Te Mana o te Wai from freshwater regulation and prevent equivalent requirements returning under another name.

policies.title: Prevent a return of Significant Natural Area rules
policies.summary: Protect farmers from a return of Labour-style Significant Natural Area rules.

policies.title: Biodiversity credits and QEII conservation
policies.summary: Expand voluntary conservation through biodiversity credits and the QEII National Trust.

policies.title: $13.5m annual rural catchment-group funding
policies.summary: Redirect $4.5 million a year of existing MPI spending to keep rural catchment-group funding at $13.5 million annually, with further funding possible for demonstrated water-quality results.

policies.title: Practical freshwater farm plans
policies.summary: Keep freshwater farm plans practical and affordable, focused on genuine environmental risks.

policies.title: Forest owners carry long-term forest costs
policies.summary: Require permanent forest owners to carry their forests' long-term costs and risks, including sufficient pest control.

policies.title: Higher penalties for illegal dumping
policies.summary: Set illegal-dumping fines at $1,000 and $2,000 for repeat offenders.

policies.title: Keep agriculture permanently outside the ETS
policies.summary: Keep agriculture permanently out of the Emissions Trading Scheme and oppose agricultural emissions taxes or pricing schemes.

policies.title: Treat methane differently from carbon dioxide
policies.summary: Recognise the different warming effects of methane and carbon dioxide in climate policy.

policies.title: Remove the ETS price floor
policies.summary: Remove the Emissions Trading Scheme price floor that supports carbon prices and encourages blanket carbon farming.

policies.title: Recognise overseas agricultural-product approvals
policies.summary: Speed access to agricultural chemicals and veterinary medicines by recognising approvals from trusted overseas regulators.

policies.title: Reduce restrictions on agricultural drones
policies.summary: Remove unnecessary restrictions on agricultural drones and barriers to new farming technology.

policies.title: Easier direct farm-product sales
policies.summary: Reduce homekill red tape and make it easier for farmers to sell their products directly to consumers.

policies.title: 24-hour prescription collection lockers
policies.summary: Enable secure electronic lockers so rural patients can collect eligible pre-dispensed medicines outside pharmacy opening hours.

policies.title: Remove the economic imperative for conservation land
policies.summary: Remove the Coalition Government's economic imperative for public conservation land so it is managed for nature rather than profit.

policies.title: Evidence-based ecosystem health limits
policies.summary: Put strong evidence-based limits in place to protect ecosystem health.

policies.title: Tangata whenua shared decision-making in resource management
policies.summary: Affirm Te Tiriti and the role of tangata whenua as shared decision-makers and kaitiaki in the new resource-management system.

policies.title: Nutrition education from primary school to medical school
policies.summary: Promote nutrition education from primary school through to medical education.

policies.title: Independent review of dietary guidelines
policies.summary: Commission a full independent review of New Zealand's dietary guidelines.

policies.title: Reduce GP administration and restore clinical autonomy
policies.summary: Reduce administrative burdens in general practice and restore professional autonomy for GPs.

policies.title: Health coaches in primary care
policies.summary: Support general practices by bringing health coaches into primary care.

policies.title: Research nutritional interventions for mental illness
policies.summary: Fund New Zealand scientists to assess nutritional interventions for preventing and treating mental illness.

policies.title: Remove barriers to recognised safe nutrients
policies.summary: Remove Medsafe and Pharmac barriers to nutrients recognised as safe.

policies.title: Hospital trials of intravenous vitamin C
policies.summary: Fund hospital trials of intravenous vitamin C before and after surgery to assess its effectiveness in preventing and treating infections.

policies.title: Review optimal vitamin D levels
policies.summary: Fund a review of vitamin D to determine optimal levels for maintaining health.

policies.title: Agricultural innovation and alternatives to harmful sprays
policies.summary: Invest in agricultural innovation for productivity, soil health, sustainability and resilience while researching practical alternatives to potentially harmful sprays.

policies.title: Support organic producers and markets
policies.summary: Reduce unnecessary barriers for organic producers, encourage investment and innovation, and grow markets for New Zealand organic products.

policies.title: Recognise the State of Palestine
policies.summary: Recognise the State of Palestine.

policies.title: Economic sanctions on Israel
policies.summary: Impose economic sanctions on Israel.

policies.title: Divest public funds from listed occupied-territory companies
policies.summary: Require the NZ Super Fund and ACC to divest holdings in companies on the UN list of businesses operating in the occupied territories.

policies.title: Support South Africa’s ICJ genocide case
policies.summary: Intervene in support of South Africa's case at the International Court of Justice concerning a breach of the Genocide Convention.

policies.title: Ban lethal fully autonomous weapons
policies.summary: Advocate for an ICJ advisory opinion on the legality of lethal fully autonomous weapons and support international efforts to ban them.

policies.title: Parliamentary scrutiny for joining armed conflicts
policies.summary: Establish clear parliamentary scrutiny if New Zealand joins armed conflicts.

policies.title: Stronger oversight of New Zealand space payloads
policies.summary: Strengthen oversight of payloads launched from New Zealand to ensure compliance with current law.

policies.title: Safe-haven programme for human rights defenders
policies.summary: Establish a programme offering safe haven to human rights defenders who face acute targeting.

policies.title: Pacific climate adaptation and displacement agreement
policies.summary: Work toward a Pacific agreement on climate mitigation, adaptation and displacement, including long-term adaptation and resettlement work with Kiribati and Tuvalu.

policies.title: Increase overseas development assistance toward 0.7% of GNI
policies.summary: Progressively increase overseas development assistance toward 0.7% of GNI as fiscal conditions allow.

policies.title: Easier movement of money and data across the Pacific
policies.summary: Support closer Pacific economic integration and make moving money and data across the Pacific easier and cheaper.

policies.title: Independent Takatāpui-governed Commission
policies.summary: Establish an independent Takatāpui-governed Commission with authority over guaranteed, ring-fenced Takatāpui-specific funding.

policies.title: $200 million Mana Takatāpui investment
policies.summary: Invest $200 million over three years across healthcare, mental health, housing, safety, education and culture, including direct investment in Takatāpui-led organisations.

policies.title: Cut eligible student-loan balances by 10%
policies.summary: Cut eligible student-loan balances by 10%; existing graduates who missed Fees Free receive the cut on 1 April 2027, while current and future students qualify after remaining in New Zealand for three years after study.

policies.title: Wipe eligible student-loan balances of $2,000 or less
policies.summary: Write off student-loan balances of $2,000 or less for borrowers eligible under Labour's student-debt reduction policy.

policies.title: 20% company tax rate for SMEs
policies.summary: Reduce the company tax rate from 28% to 20% for businesses with annual turnover below $30 million.

policies.title: Replace the Waitangi Tribunal with a completion commission
policies.summary: Introduce legislation within the first 100 days to abolish the Waitangi Tribunal and replace it with a commission tasked with finalising claims arising before 2008.

policies.title: Prioritise Māori land reform
policies.summary: Prioritise Māori land reform and administrative improvements in the Māori Land Court.

policies.title: Move Crown–Māori and settlement work to the Ministry of Māori Development
policies.summary: Make a strengthened Ministry of Māori Development responsible for settlement implementation, contemporary claims, post-settlement leadership and Crown–Māori relations.

policies.title: Simplify FBT vehicle record-keeping
policies.summary: Remove the requirement for employers to keep detailed fringe-benefit-tax log books for work vehicles.

policies.title: Pay R&D tax credits during the year
policies.summary: Allow innovative firms to receive research-and-development tax credits during the year rather than after it.

policies.title: Double the foreign investment fund threshold
policies.summary: Double the threshold at which overseas shares become subject to the foreign investment fund tax rules.

policies.title: Open government procurement supplier panels
policies.summary: Open currently closed government supplier panels so more businesses can compete for over $50 billion of annual government purchasing.

policies.title: Coordinate regulation to enable new fintech
policies.summary: Coordinate regulation across the Reserve Bank, MBIE and the Financial Markets Authority to reduce bureaucracy and barriers to new financial technology.

policies.title: Rewrite health and safety codes in plain English
policies.summary: Rewrite health and safety codes in plain English to make compliance more straightforward.

policies.title: Replace NCEA with subject exams and A+ to E grades
policies.summary: Replace NCEA with A+ to E grades and an examination in every subject.

policies.title: Double Trades Academy places to 20,000
policies.summary: Double Trades Academy places to 20,000 by 2030.

policies.title: Introduce nine industry-developed vocational subjects
policies.summary: Roll out nine new vocational subjects and courses developed with industry.

policies.title: Review tax settings for Active Investor Plus visa holders
policies.summary: Ensure foreign investment fund settings and Inland Revenue rules do not discourage Active Investor Plus visa holders from remaining in New Zealand and investing in the economy.

policies.title: Legislate infrastructure asset-management and capital plans
policies.summary: Legislate requirements for infrastructure asset-management plans and long-term capital plans.

policies.title: Internationally cost-benchmark government infrastructure
policies.summary: Require the Infrastructure Commission to internationally cost-benchmark government-led transport, school and hospital projects.

policies.title: Cap council rates increases
policies.summary: Implement a rates cap intended to limit large increases in council costs.

policies.title: Ban junk car insurance
policies.summary: Ban junk car insurance products such as paint insurance and mechanical breakdown cover with broad exclusions.

policies.title: Stop hard-selling extended warranties
policies.summary: Stop the hard sell of extended warranties on electronics and whiteware at the checkout.

policies.title: Upfront pricing for mandatory fees
policies.summary: Require all mandatory fees, including ticket-sale fees, to be included in the price shown upfront.

policies.title: Easy cancellation for subscriptions and gym memberships
policies.summary: Require subscription services and gym memberships to be as easy to cancel as they are to start.

policies.title: Ban unfair phone and internet contract terms
policies.summary: Ban unfair exit fees, excessive notice periods and unclear auto-renewals on phone and internet contracts, and require the full price upfront.

policies.title: Mandatory lobbyist code and public register
policies.summary: Introduce a mandatory code of conduct for paid lobbyists and a public register showing who they are and who pays them.

policies.title: Stand-down period before former ministers can lobby
policies.summary: Introduce a stand-down period before former ministers can move from Cabinet into paid lobbying work.

policies.title: Restrict urgency and require later select-committee review
policies.summary: Restrict urgency to specified circumstances and automatically send laws passed under urgency to a select committee within six months.

policies.title: Modernise the Official Information Act
policies.summary: Codify proactive information releases, including ministers' diaries, and create penalties for breaches of the Official Information Act.

policies.title: Restore election-day enrolment
policies.summary: Restore the ability of eligible people to enrol and vote on election day.

policies.title: Voting at 16 in local elections
policies.summary: Give 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote in local elections.

policies.title: One person, one vote in local elections
policies.summary: End the rule that allows some property owners to vote in more than one council area.

policies.title: Equal donation disclosure for third-party campaigners
policies.summary: Require third-party campaigners in local and national elections to disclose donations on the same terms as political parties.

policies.title: Restore pay equity legislation
policies.summary: Restore pay equity legislation in the first 100 days and accommodate work already completed on claims.

policies.title: $4 hourly pay rise for care and support workers
policies.summary: Increase pay for about 65,000 care and support workers by $4 an hour from 1 January 2027.

policies.title: Restore pay equity and fund care-worker settlement
policies.summary: Restore the pre-2025 pay equity law and set aside about $1.1 billion a year for a negotiated settlement covering roughly 65,000 care and support workers.

policies.title: Free and capped public-transport fares
policies.summary: Make bus and train fares free for children, teenagers, students, apprentices, Community Service Card holders and Total Mobility users, with a maximum $2 adult fare.

policies.title: Mass rapid transit in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch
policies.summary: Build mass rapid bus and light-rail systems in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch.

policies.title: Fund council public-transport service shortfalls
policies.summary: Fund council public-transport shortfalls to improve services in smaller cities, towns and major metropolitan areas.

policies.title: More frequent inter-regional bus services
policies.summary: Deliver more frequent, affordable inter-regional bus services connecting smaller cities and towns.

policies.title: Intercity passenger rail services
policies.summary: Provide an Auckland-Wellington overnight train, restore Christchurch-Dunedin passenger rail with a possible Invercargill extension, and improve, electrify and extend Te Huia to Tauranga.

policies.title: Enable more inner-city pedestrianisation
policies.summary: Enable councils to pedestrianise more inner-city areas to support urban revitalisation and safe walking and cycling.

policies.title: Energy development zones with user-funded transmission
policies.summary: Allow developers, major electricity users and investors to build transmission in new energy development zones and recover costs from users.

policies.title: Choice of accredited electricity connection contractor
policies.summary: Allow electricity customers to choose an accredited contractor to complete connection work instead of using only their network's contractor.

policies.title: Sell distributed electricity to any power company
policies.summary: Allow households and businesses with solar or batteries to sell electricity to any power company, not only their retailer.

policies.title: Open the backup electricity market
policies.summary: Open the backup-power market so smaller electricity retailers can obtain supply for dry years.

policies.title: Review lines charges and fast-track small solar connections
policies.summary: Review the rules governing electricity lines charges and require residential and small-business solar connections to be approved within two working days.

policies.title: Electricity affordability as a statutory objective
policies.summary: Write electricity affordability into law as a core objective of the Electricity Authority.

policies.title: Cut consenting barriers for renewable generation
policies.summary: Reduce regulatory barriers so wind, solar and hydro generation can be built faster.

policies.title: Seamless trans-Tasman travel trial
policies.summary: Work with Australia on a pre-October 2028 trial using digital credentials and biometrics to streamline travel for eligible Australian and New Zealand citizens while retaining border controls.

policies.title: Start Mill Road Stage One construction
policies.summary: Allocate $1.75 billion in Budget 2028 to begin construction of Mill Road Stage One between Manukau and Alfriston in the late-2028 construction season.

policies.title: Protect routes for Mill Road Stages Two and Three
policies.summary: Allocate $100 million to progress route protection for Mill Road Stages Two and Three.

policies.title: First Employee Support Package
policies.summary: Provide first-year employment-agreement, payroll, tax, ACC and leave guidance for first-time employers, with reduced penalties for genuine administrative mistakes that cause no worker harm.

policies.title: Recurring seasonal employment agreement
policies.summary: Create a standard recurring seasonal agreement and shorter renewal process while retaining the requirement for a genuine seasonal reason.

policies.title: Digital apprenticeship competency records
policies.summary: Require consistent acceptance of approved digital competency records and electronic supervisor sign-off for apprenticeships.

policies.title: Employment Leave Act transition support
policies.summary: Provide early guidance, worked payroll examples and coordinated implementation support before the new leave system starts in August 2028.

policies.title: Review the GST registration threshold
policies.summary: Review the compulsory GST registration threshold to reduce compliance and remove barriers to small-business growth while considering fiscal impacts.

policies.title: Fast-track minor employment disputes
policies.summary: Create a simplified Employment Relations Authority pathway for suitable minor disputes with clear eligibility and firm decision timeframes.

policies.title: Offer mediation options for minor employment disputes
policies.summary: Require available mediator recommendations and binding options to be clearly explained and offered in suitable minor disputes.

policies.title: One-month ERA determination deadline
policies.summary: Require Employment Relations Authority determinations within one month of the investigation meeting or final submissions, except in exceptional circumstances.

policies.title: Reuse recorded oral evidence from the ERA
policies.summary: Require reliable recording of oral evidence in the Employment Relations Authority so it can be reused where lawful and fair.

policies.title: Strengthen ERA case-management powers
policies.summary: Strengthen Employment Relations Authority powers to narrow issues, direct relevant information and deal with unnecessary procedural delay.

policies.title: Review ERA enforcement powers
policies.summary: Review whether the Employment Relations Authority should be able to enforce more of its own orders without separate court proceedings.

policies.title: Regulate paid employment advocates
policies.summary: Introduce proportionate conduct, competence, fee-transparency and complaints requirements for paid employment advocates.

policies.title: Employee-support threshold for collective bargaining
policies.summary: Require support from the lesser of 10 employees or 20% of those proposed to be covered, with a minimum of two, before new collective bargaining begins.

policies.title: Early employment-status determination
policies.summary: Create an early process for resolving disputed employee status under section 6 of the Employment Relations Act.

policies.title: Employment Relations Consolidation Bill
policies.summary: Prepare and introduce legislation consolidating core employment law into a clearer framework.

policies.title: Tell Government Once service
policies.summary: Let businesses update core details once through an NZBN-based service and securely share the changes with participating agencies and councils.

policies.title: Coordinated and simplified business renewals
policies.summary: Coordinate business permit and licence renewals and introduce automatic or simplified renewals for suitable low-risk businesses with strong compliance records.

policies.title: Reform alcohol-licensing applications and renewals
policies.summary: Simplify alcohol-licence applications and renewals, extend suitable renewal periods and reform fees.

policies.title: Allow accountants to administer statutory declarations
policies.summary: Allow eligible chartered accountants to administer statutory declarations with professional and identity safeguards.

policies.title: Digital-first business records and notices
policies.summary: Remove unjustified paper, physical-display, newspaper, fax and telex requirements where secure and accessible digital alternatives are suitable.

policies.title: Clearer small-business fire-safety guidance
policies.summary: Publish clearer guidance and templates for small-business fire-evacuation requirements and approved schemes.

policies.title: Enforce government prompt-payment performance
policies.summary: Hold agencies accountable for slow payment and enforce fair payment terms through government procurement supply chains.

policies.title: Expand eInvoicing and prompt-payment code
policies.summary: Complete the industry-led prompt-payment programme and expand eInvoicing with business and accounting organisations.

policies.title: Transparent and lower payment fees
policies.summary: Improve payment-fee transparency, monitor whether regulated savings reach merchants and support further evidence-based fee reductions.

policies.title: Complete open banking and payments modernisation
policies.summary: Complete regulated open banking and the Reserve Bank payments-modernisation programme.

policies.title: Independent access to motor-vehicle repair information
policies.summary: Give independent vehicle repairers regulated access to manufacturers' repair information with safety, security and commercial safeguards.

policies.title: Expand AI support for small businesses
policies.summary: Expand co-funded practical AI support for small businesses, including the AI Advisory Pilot.

policies.title: Reuse certified engineering and geotechnical reports
policies.summary: Require regulators to reuse current, relevant certified engineering and geotechnical reports where they remain fit for purpose.

policies.title: Next 200 exporter support
policies.summary: Give 200 high-potential small and medium exporters intensive NZTE support, market intelligence, introductions and regulatory assistance.

policies.title: AI-powered export navigator
policies.summary: Create official AI-assisted tools covering tariffs, rules of origin and market-access requirements.

policies.title: Trusted-exporter fast lane
policies.summary: Create a Secure Exports Scheme fast lane for eligible smaller exporters and reduce duplicated documentation.

policies.title: Keep Investment Boost
policies.summary: Retain the immediate 20% deduction for eligible productive assets for businesses of every size.

policies.title: Consolidate building-consent functions
policies.summary: Enable greater consolidation of building-consent functions and more consistent decisions.

policies.title: Halve Project Information Memorandum processing time
policies.summary: Reduce Project Information Memorandum processing time from 20 to 10 working days.

policies.title: Proportionate building liability and home warranties
policies.summary: Introduce proportionate building liability backed by professional indemnity insurance and home warranties.

policies.title: Recognise trusted overseas building products
policies.summary: Expand recognition of trusted overseas building products and standards that meet New Zealand requirements.

policies.title: Make capital raising easier for growing firms
policies.summary: Reform capital-market requirements so growing firms can raise equity and debt more easily while retaining investor protections.

policies.title: Connect businesses with international investment
policies.summary: Use Invest New Zealand to connect productive businesses with international investment, skills and commercial partners.

policies.title: Increase Pharmac medicines budget by $604 million
policies.summary: Provide a further $604 million uplift to Pharmac's medicines budget to fund new medicines and widen access to funded treatments.

policies.title: Reduce non-Pacific foreign aid to fund medicines
policies.summary: Reduce foreign aid and associated administration outside the Pacific by 10%, while protecting Pacific aid, to help fund medicines.

policies.title: Set a national clinical-trials target
policies.summary: Set a national target for clinical trials conducted in New Zealand.

policies.title: Unlock CAR-T cell therapy
policies.summary: Expand access to CAR-T cell therapy in New Zealand.

policies.title: Lower free bowel-screening age to 50
policies.summary: Lower the eligibility age for free bowel screening to 50 by 2029 and expand colonoscopy capacity.

policies.title: Extend free breast screening to age 74
policies.summary: Complete the extension of free breast screening to age 74 by 2029.

policies.title: Pilot prostate and lung cancer screening
policies.summary: Launch organised screening pilots for prostate and lung cancer to assess potential nationwide programmes.

policies.title: Free cervical screening for ages 25 to 69
policies.summary: Provide free cervical screening for women aged 25 to 69 from March 2027.

policies.title: Healthy Kiwis active-prescription programme
policies.summary: Offer active prescriptions through a Healthy Kiwis Programme and double participation by 2030.

policies.title: Fund Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass
policies.summary: Commit $800 million in the first Budget to fully fund the motorway and bypass so construction can start in 2027.

policies.title: Right to repair for motor vehicles
policies.summary: Require vehicle manufacturers to give independent mechanics fair access to the manuals, software, tools and information needed to repair modern vehicles.

policies.title: Weekly fuel-price reporting
policies.summary: Require the Commerce Commission to report weekly on fuel prices and whether falling wholesale costs are being passed on to drivers.

policies.title: Apply price-gouging law to fuel
policies.summary: Apply price-gouging rules to wholesale and retail fuel, allowing unfair pricing to be investigated and overcharges recovered.

policies.title: Fairer wholesale fuel access for independent stations
policies.summary: Give independent petrol stations fairer access to fuel supplies and stronger protection against restrictive contracts.

policies.title: Use surplus NZTA land for independent fuel and EV sites
policies.summary: Require NZTA to consider making surplus land available for independent unmanned petrol stations and EV chargers.

policies.title: Remove ring-net fishing exemption in Hauraki Gulf
policies.summary: Immediately remove the ring-net fishing exemption from Hauraki Gulf High Protection Areas.

policies.title: Phase out bottom trawling starting with ecologically significant areas
policies.summary: Phase out bottom trawling, starting with seamounts and ecologically significant areas including the Hauraki Gulf.

policies.title: Protect 30% of Hauraki Gulf by 2030
policies.summary: Protect 30% of the Hauraki Gulf by 2030 as part of a plan to protect at least 30% of New Zealand's ocean.

policies.title: Resource iwi and hapū-led ocean protection
policies.summary: Embed kaitiakitanga Māori in marine management and resource iwi and hapū to lead ocean-protection work.

policies.title: Increase marine biosecurity resourcing
policies.summary: Increase resources for marine biosecurity.

policies.title: Cameras and mortality limits to reduce fisheries bycatch
policies.summary: Roll out cameras on fishing boats and set fisheries-related mortality limits to reduce bycatch.

policies.title: Review Quota Management System for ecosystem health
policies.summary: Review the Quota Management System so fisheries can be managed according to whole-ecosystem health.

policies.title: Stop Hauraki Gulf pollution at source
policies.summary: Strengthen wastewater-discharge rules and phase out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser to reduce pollution reaching the Hauraki Gulf.

policies.title: Remove charitable-donation tax-credit cap
policies.summary: Remove the $33,333 cap on tax benefits available for charitable donations.

policies.title: Random drug testing for work-ready Jobseekers
policies.summary: Start with 10,000 random tests in the first year, record a first failed test and require a clinical assessment after a second failure before ordinary obligations and sanctions apply.

policies.title: Earlier intensive support for long-term Jobseekers
policies.summary: Provide intensive work-focused support to 30,000 work-ready people who have received Jobseeker for more than a year.

policies.title: Lower Jobseeker rate after two years
policies.summary: From 1 April 2028, move people who received Jobseeker for two of the previous three years to a lower payment rate, with a smaller reduction for households with dependent children.

policies.title: Longer stand-down for repeated voluntary unemployment
policies.summary: Increase the non-entitlement period from 13 to 26 weeks for people who repeatedly leave work without good and sufficient reason.

policies.title: Five-year residence requirement for main benefits
policies.summary: From 1 April 2028, increase the minimum residence period for main-benefit eligibility from two years to five years.

policies.title: Concessional loans for water storage
policies.summary: Commit $300 million in concessional loans for water storage, beginning with five prioritised projects.

policies.title: Long-term water infrastructure pipeline
policies.summary: Develop New Zealand's first long-term water infrastructure pipeline with growers, farmers, councils and iwi.

policies.title: National Rural and Provincial Water Use Strategy
policies.summary: Publish a national rural and provincial water-use strategy in 2027, supported by a national storage register.

policies.title: National standard for lower-risk water storage
policies.summary: Introduce a national standard for on-farm and other lower-risk off-stream water storage.

policies.title: National irrigation consenting standard
policies.summary: Introduce a national irrigation standard to simplify consenting for farmers and growers.

policies.title: Fertiliser security agreements
